body.en: *Bubble sort* compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. After the first pass the largest element has bubbled to the last position; after pass k the last k elements are in place. An array of n elements needs at most n − 1 passes. If a pass makes no swap, the array is already sorted and we can stop early.

body.en: *Selection sort* finds the smallest element of the unsorted part and swaps it into the first position of that part. Pass 1 puts the smallest element at index 0, pass 2 the next smallest at index 1, and so on: n − 1 passes in all. It makes at most one swap per pass (n − 1 swaps), while bubble sort may make many; both make about n²/2 comparisons.
